@graph.name: Richmond Marine Terminal Logistics Dataset
@graph.description: The per-port dataset for Richmond Marine Terminal in the Ports & Intermodal program of The Flat Rate Movers: the full port record for the James River barge terminal at 5000 Deepwater Terminal Rd, Richmond, VA — owned by the City of Richmond, leased by the Virginia Port Authority under a 40-year lease signed 2016 (to 2056) and operated by Virginia International Terminals, LLC as part of the Port of Virginia system — 124 acres with 300,000 sq ft of storage, a mobile harbor crane in the 124-ton class, three reefer plugs, a Monday-Friday 0700-1600 gate, on-terminal transload and cross-docking, CSX direct rail with Norfolk Southern via local switch, and the Richmond Express (64 Express) barge service: three barges in rotation, 500 FEU combined capacity, running six days a week with about a 12-hour overnight transit to Norfolk International Terminals, the Virginia International Gateway and Portsmouth Marine Terminal. No standalone annual volume is published for this terminal. The I-95, I-64, I-85 and I-295 corridors, and the branch binding: the terminal is served from the Winchester, VA branch, about 135 road miles away (Martinsburg measures about 158). The company's eight attached port services are recorded cell by cell in the companion coverage dataset. No port tenancy or port-authority relationship is claimed; the company's crews hold TWIC cards and its contractors hold valid TWIC cards.

@graph.name: Richmond Marine Terminal Service Coverage Dataset
@graph.description: The service-coverage cells for the Richmond Marine Terminal in the Ports & Intermodal program: the eight attached services (transloading; ocean container packing and unpacking; loading and unloading / container labor; cross-docking; freight rework; specialized workforce; logistics project management; 3PL support services), each recorded as offered with its delivery points (port-adjacent warehouse, receiver's dock, yard, leased space, and on-terminal by arrangement — on-terminal work happens only by arrangement through the terminal's own processes, never as a bare claim) and its bound branch, Winchester, VA. Drayage is not offered at any port in the program.

@graph.name: Richmond Marine Terminal
@graph.description: Richmond Marine Terminal (Richmond, VA) — river barge terminal (inland port). Authority: Virginia Port Authority (operator under lease). Operator: Virginia International Terminals, LLC — the City of Richmond owns the terminal; the Virginia Port Authority leases it under a 40-year lease signed 2016 (to 2056). Cargo: barge containers on the Richmond Express (64 Express) James River barge service linking Richmond with NIT, VIG and PMT; breakbulk. Rail: CSX — direct; Norfolk Southern — via local switch. Highway corridors: I-95, I-64, I-85, I-295. Branch binding: this port is served from the Winchester, VA branch of The Flat Rate Movers — about 135 road miles from Winchester and 158 from Martinsburg; bound to Winchester on miles. about 23 mi / about 20 min closer from Winchester; secondary node (section of the Port of Virginia hub, no dedicated hub page or dataset file in wave 1).
